Pretty wacky game, Love a lot. Its a good game to play with friends, you CAN play it alone, but its really difficult. Lots of content in it as well. Graphic is not the best but it does a good job conveying the DESTRUCTION. 

Yes you can casually commit war crimes but don't worry! You look cool while doing it.

In this review I will be talking about EDF 5, and also giving a bit of a comparison of 5 to the previous one in the series, 4.1.

EDF 5 is a third person shooter. It is mission based. Each mission has a specific set of enemy and enemy types in a specific environment. Overall the mission objectives are largely the same, in that you must destroy all enemies. However, the enemy types vary greatly. This means that while the overall goal of the game seems similar, the variety in enemies will mean that missions don't feel the same in terms of gameplay particulars. To give an example. A starting enemy is a giant ant. The ants have a close range projectile. Another variant, with a different colour, does not have a projectile, but will charge you and try to grab you and bite you. Then you may have a spider, which will jump around and fire long range projectiles that can trap you.

Enemies have distinct attacks, and are easily identifiable, and there are clear ways of dealing with each one. So while you are facing hordes and waves of enemies, you have clear understanding of what you are trying to do, and coming up with strategies, rather than being crushed by unclear gameplay mechanics.

The weapon types are where there is big variety. There are a large variety of weapon types, and they are mostly generally useful. Some weapons are better than others, and some are much more efficient than others, but alot of types are a resonable choice in a given situation. 

The other element giving variety is the class system. There are four classes, and they are quite distinct from each other. 

The Ranger is the basic soldier, who has access to the most straightforward weapons, but is still effective. They aren't as fast as some of the others, but they are more straightforward, in that you don't have to make resource use decisions or time weapon attacks. They are just generally effective.

The Wing Diver has a jet pack to fly and hover. They also have some weird and wonderful weapon types. However, the power pack they have that powers their flight also powers their guns. So while they have very high mobility, and attack damage, they also have to make decisions of when to shoot and when to fly, and where to land, because they can overload their energy and have to wait many seconds with no power while their power recharges.

Air Raider are like Rangers, but with lower mobility and toughness, and close quarter combat ability, but with bigger weapons and the ability to summon vehicles. By bigger weapons, I mean they can summon air raids, bombing runs, giant missiles, satellite laser attacks. They can also summon tanks and mechs for themselves or rangers to drive.

Fencers are people who wear powered suits. They suits give them higher defence, and mobility. This mobility, which high, is also restricted, in that it is big dashes and boosted jumps. So while they are fast, they are also making hops and jumps around the place, that need to be decided upon in advance. Their weapons are big and powerful, requiring the powered suits strength to operate, but they are also slow starting and require one to basically stand still and not move to fire. So the high mobility and slow weapons combine to mean that you move quickly to a position, fire off some shots, and then move quickly to another location and do it again. They can be very rhythmic.

The sheer variety of weapons, and class differences, means that there are a lot of variety in how one approaches a given scenario. Each weapon is usually quite distinct from another. There can be big differences in shot types, speed, and ammo consumption, so you have to spend a bit of time learn each weapon as to be effective with it. And you have to make some decisions of gun type based on the enemies you will face.

In comparison to EDF 4.1 5 is a general upgrade in basically every area. More weapons are effective and balanced. The classes are made more generally effective and don't have the sometimes massive weaknesses they did in 4.1. Missions were changed so that they don’t only reward highly specialised loadouts like 4.1

The only thing I think is generally worse in 5, compared to 4.1, is the story. 4.1 feels really coherent, like each mission lead on from the last one, you are fighting harder enemies, and like the situation is evolving and leading to a massive final confrontation. 5 feels like you are going to random locations and fighting some random group. It doesn't have that build up feel, and it doesn't feel very continuous.  The early missions for 5 can be kind of boring for a while. 4.1 starts off right in the action.

EDF 5 also has co-op. It has both types of co-op, both online for 4 players, and local coop for 2 players. Coop works very well in this game, because you can choose weapons and classes in relation to eachother. It's the good type of Co-op game where players are rewarded for working together, while also allowing people alot of freedom in what they choose to do, or how they choose to play. 

There is an element of grinding. You get new weapons and weapon upgrades from boxes, and extra armour(life). Boxes have a chance of dropping from each enemy. You have to physically pick up a box to get its contents, as it won't just give you everything that dropped in a mission. This might be very frustrating to players.  I found that if you just try to pick up as many boxes as possible during the missions, that you could complete the game without redoing missions multiple times to get more armour or guns.


I highly recommend EDF 5. It is well balanced and very gameplay focused. It might look like a basic horde shooting game, but you have classes that play completely differently in terms of weapons and mobility, very unique weapon types, and lots of different enemy types that are all clear and able to be understood, while still providing a reasonable challenge. You need to think about your weapon choices and tactics. It is very engaging in terms of gameplay.

Japanese Left 4 Dead
2010 graphics, cheesy voice acting, simple story, Fun gameplay loop.  Awesome Coop experience

Finally, a game that knows it's a game.
10/10.
